# browser-mcp

A Playwright-backed Model Context Protocol server providing browser primitives plus domain plugins for design audits, WordPress block development, and Gutenberg authoring.

This file is the consumer-facing manual for agents that *invoke* browser-mcp tools. If you're building or extending the server itself, read the source — this file omits per-line code detail and stays at the contract surface, with source-tree pointers (§ Plugins and modes) for finding the implementation behind a behavior.

## TL;DR {#tldr}

- Browser primitives (navigate, click, screenshot, evaluate, ...) plus four pluggable domains: `dev`, `design-compare`, `wp`, `wp-gutenberg`. Each plugin registers tools.
- A **mode** is a session-level auth/setup bundle that a plugin can also register (e.g. `wp` registers the `wordpress` mode that injects WordPress admin auth into the BrowserContext). Modes are NOT a gate on which tools are available — they layer hooks onto sessions. `mcp__browser__list_modes` enumerates registered modes.
- Tools accept an optional `session_id` to attach to a persistent context (from `open_session`); without it each call spins an ephemeral session and discards it on return.
- Comparison tools (`compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `visual_diff`, `design_audit`) report different score conventions and accept different mask APIs — see § Cross-cutting concepts before mixing them.
- `align_elements` is a measurement tool, not a comparison tool: it returns the per-element (dx, dy) translation that best matches the reference, grounded in pixel SAD over the live screenshot. Use it when DOM-reported coordinates are suspect — see § Surfaces › `align_elements`.
- All coordinates the tool produces or consumes are **HTML viewport pixels**. Values from non-viewport sources (Figma canvas, Figma node-relative) carry their own coordinate frame and must be converted before they cross the API boundary — see § Coordinate spaces.

## Plugins and modes {#modes-and-plugins}

The server boots with a plugin set defined by the `BROWSER_MCP_PLUGINS` env var (comma-separated, e.g. `dev,wp,wp-gutenberg,design-compare`). Each plugin can:

- **Register tools** (the `mcp__browser__*` surface). A tool is available whenever its registering plugin is loaded — there's no per-tool mode gate.
- **Register modes** as session-level auth/setup bundles. A mode is a set of hooks (e.g. inject auth cookies before any tool runs in this session) that consumers opt into per session. Currently the `wp` plugin registers the `wordpress` mode (WordPress admin auth injection); no other plugin registers a mode.
- **Declare required env vars and dependencies** on other plugins.

**Tolerant loader.** A plugin with a missing required env var is silently skipped, and its dependents cascade-skip (e.g. `wp-gutenberg` skips when `wp` skips for a missing `WP_URL`). Stderr carries the warning; the server still boots and unaffected plugins still work. Hard errors only fire on real config bugs (sealed registry, name collision, undeclared dependency, tool/action/mode collision).

> **Hazard:** if `mcp__browser__list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or an expected mode is missing, the cause is almost always a silently-skipped plugin from missing env. See § Diagnosis › Mode not registered for the fix recipe.

**MCP scopes replace, do not merge.** When the same server name (`browser`) appears in both `~/.claude.json` (user scope) and a project-local `.mcp.json`, the project entry **fully replaces** the user entry. There is no env-block merge. If a project needs a different `WP_URL`, the project entry must duplicate the full env block, not just the override.

**Where plugins live in source.** `src/plugins/dev`, `src/plugins/design-compare`, `src/plugins/wp`, `src/plugins/wp-gutenberg`. Plugin manifests at `src/plugins/<name>/index.ts`. Tool implementations under `src/plugins/<name>/tools/` (or `src/core/` for primitives). The plugin registry (`src/plugins/registry.ts`) enforces the dependency graph and the cascade-skip behavior.

## Command index {#command-index}

Exhaustive list of `mcp__browser__*` tools by plugin. Tools marked **(contract)** have a deep treatment in § Surfaces; the rest are routine and have a one-line entry only. Use this table to pick the right tool, then dive to the contract section if the tool is non-trivial.

### dev plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `screenshot` | Full-page or clipped PNG screenshot | core primitive |
| `element_screenshot` | Element-bbox-cropped screenshot | core primitive |
| `visual_diff` | Pixelmatch two PNGs, optional crop | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `compare_screenshot` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, full-page | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, coverage |
| `compare_element` | Live URL ↔ reference PNG, element-cropped | (contract) compare-tool selection, mask, alignment, coverage |
| `align_elements` | Per-element pixel-shift measurement vs reference PNG; applies CSS transforms to confirm | (contract) align-vs-compare selection |
| `console_capture` | Capture console messages over a script run | |
| `dom_snapshot` | Full DOM tree as JSON | |
| `accessibility_snapshot` | a11y tree | |
| `network_log` | HAR-style network requests over a script run | |
| `page_metadata` | Title, URL, meta tags | |
| `performance_metrics` | LCP, FCP, TTFB | |
| `computed_styles` | `getComputedStyle()` for selector | |
| `evaluate_script` | Run JS in page context, return result | |
| `trace_start` / `trace_stop` | Playwright trace zip | |
| `schema_extract` | JSON-LD / microdata / OG tags | |

### design-compare plugin

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `design_compare` | CSS-property comparison live ↔ design spec | (contract) compare-tool selection |
| `design_audit` | `design_compare` + visual diff + cross-reference | (contract) compare-tool selection, hide, coverage |

| Tool | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|

| `list_modes` | enumerate registered modes |

## Cross-cutting concepts {#cross-cutting}

### Coordinate spaces {#coordinate-spaces}

browser-mcp deals exclusively in **HTML viewport pixels** at every API boundary:

- `getBoundingClientRect()` — what the tool internally calls — returns viewport-relative coordinates, post-transform.
- The reference PNG passed to `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot` is treated as image-pixel space, which is 1:1 with HTML viewport when the screenshot was captured at the same dimensions (the tool defaults `viewport` to the reference image's dimensions to enforce this).
- `ignoreRegions[].x/y/width/height` — image-pixel coords.
- `alignOn.referenceRect` — image-pixel coords.
- `coverageManifest` — names and counts only; no coordinates.

> **Conversion rule** (mirrors `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces`): values from non-viewport sources carry their own coordinate frame; conversion to HTML viewport is the consumer's responsibility, not auto-resolved by browser-mcp.

Non-viewport frames (canvas-relative, node-relative, layout-tree exports) come from upstream design tooling and live in distinct coordinate spaces. browser-mcp **never** auto-resolves between frames. Values supplied to a viewport-pixel field (`ignoreRegions`, `alignOn.referenceRect`, anything constructed from a `getBoundingClientRect`-equivalent on the live page) must already be in HTML viewport / image-pixel coords. Values pasted from a non-viewport frame will silently absorb the conversion offset into computed deltas and downstream comparisons drift — see § Diagnosis › Coordinate frame mismatch for the consumer-side fix recipe.

The full multi-frame treatment (canvas, node-relative, viewport, and conversion math between them) lives at `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces` — figexport is the authoritative source on the upstream side, since that's where non-viewport frames originate.

### Compare-tool selection {#compare-tool-selection}

When sources of truth disagree about which compare tool to use, the precedence is:

| Goal | Primary | Secondary | Tertiary | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Live block ↔ design reference, with property checks | `design_audit` | `design_compare` + `compare_element` separately | `compare_screenshot` | `design_audit` runs both phases and cross-references clusters to elements |
| Live element ↔ static reference image | `compare_element` | `compare_screenshot` with `ignoreRegions` | `visual_diff` after manual capture | `compare_element` anchors on selector bbox; full-page only when bbox routing fails |
| Two static PNGs, no live page | `visual_diff` | — | — | no browser launched |
| Single CSS-property check, no visual diff needed | `design_compare` | `computed_styles` + manual assert | — | `design_compare` evaluates a whole element list; `computed_styles` is one-shot |
| "How far off is this element from the reference, in pixels?" | `align_elements` | `compare_element` clusters + manual measurement | — | `align_elements` answers with a (dx, dy); `compare_element` answers with a percent + cluster bboxes |
| DOM-reported geometry is suspect (transforms, sub-pixel layout, dynamic positioning) | `align_elements` | — | — | `align_elements` only uses bbox to seed a search; the answer is grounded in pixels |

**Score conventions differ.** This is the most common cross-tool misread:

- `compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `visual_diff` report **`Diff: N.NN%`** (lower = better) plus `Match: YES/NO` against `maxDiffPercent` (default 5%).
- `design_audit` reports **`visualScore`** computed as `1 - diffPercentage/100`, range `[0, 1]`, 4 decimals (higher = better).
- `pixelmatch` threshold knob: `precise` (0.1, default for `compare_*`) or `design` (0.3, default for `design_audit`). The threshold is per-pixel sensitivity, not the score.

### Mask contract {#mask-contract}

`compare_element` and `compare_screenshot` accept pixelmatch-time mask flags:

- `ignoreImages` / `ignoreBackgrounds` — by element kind. img tags / `background-image` rules.
- `ignoreAllImages` — `ignoreImages + ignoreBackgrounds`.
- `ignoreText` — every text-line bbox via TreeWalker + Range.getClientRects.
- `ignoreElements: [{selector, mode}]` — by selector; `mode` is `"invisible"` (alpha 0) or `"position-only"` (gray fill, position still verified).
- `ignoreRegions: [{x, y, width, height, mode?, reason?}]` — manual rects.

Mask bboxes from selectors are **re-collected on every call** at the moment between screenshot capture and the post-screenshot evaluate. They follow the live element's current position. Manual `ignoreRegions` rects are static and do not.

> **Hazard (race on animation):** the screenshot via Playwright's `page.screenshot()` and the bbox query via a subsequent `page.evaluate()` are two sequential awaits with no synchronization barrier. An element animating between them desyncs the mask from the screenshot. Mitigation: inject a freeze stylesheet via `actions: [{type: "evaluate", expression: "document.head.appendChild(...)"}]` (browser-mcp has no `freezeAnimations` flag on `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot`; `design_audit` does), or use `delay` past the longest in-flight transition, or double-capture and verify ≥ 0.99 inter-screenshot diff.

> **Hazard (mask coverage trap):** masks that obscure most of the comparison region produce trivially-high match scores — when both crops have matching gray fills, pixelmatch reports near-zero diff regardless of underlying layout. The combination `ignoreAllImages: true` + `ignoreText: true` on a content-heavy block is the canonical case (most visible content masked, only wrapper background remains). The tool reports `Mask coverage: N.N%` and emits a warning when coverage > 60% with both flags active. Full symptom-and-fix at § Diagnosis › Mask coverage trap.

### Hide contract (design_audit only) {#hide-contract}

`design_audit` accepts:

- `hideSelectors: [selector]` — applies `visibility: hidden` BEFORE screenshot. Pixels are absent from the PNG entirely. `hiddenArea` reported as % of root area.
- `knownExclusions: [selector]` — post-hoc cluster classification, not masking. Diff clusters overlapping these elements get `status: "excluded"` instead of `"unexplained"`. No effect on the screenshot itself.

**`design_audit` does NOT support the `compare_element` mask API.** No `ignoreElements`, `ignoreAllImages`, `ignoreText`, or `ignoreRegions`. The analogue is `hideSelectors`, with a different mechanism (pre-screenshot suppression) and a different gate (`hiddenArea > 25%` hard-fail).

### Alignment contract {#alignment-contract}

`compare_element` accepts two mutually-exclusive alignment modes for shifting the reference crop to match the live element:

- `alignTo: "top" | "center"` — element-relative. Shifts the reference so the element's bbox lands at top-left or center.
- `alignOn: {referenceRect, frontendSelector, mode?}` — anchor-pair. Shifts the reference so a named anchor in both sides aligns.

Both compute `deltaX` / `deltaY` and apply that to the reference crop origin. `alignOn` warns when the delta exceeds 100px.

> **Hazard (coordinate frame mismatch):** `alignOn.referenceRect` is consumed as image-pixel coords (HTML viewport, 1:1 with the reference PNG). Values supplied from a different frame (e.g. canvas-relative bboxes from a Figma file) absorb their conversion offset into `deltaX`/`deltaY`, and the comparison silently drifts. The 100px warning catches gross cases but not subtle ones. Full symptom-and-fix at § Diagnosis › Coordinate frame mismatch.

### Align-vs-compare selection {#align-vs-compare-selection}

`compare_element` (and friends) and `align_elements` look superficially related but answer different questions. Pick by the question shape, not by the artifact you have in hand:

| Question | Tool | Output shape |
|---|---|---|
| "Does the live page match the reference, and where doesn't it?" | `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot` / `design_audit` | `Diff: N.NN%` + `Match: YES/NO` + cluster bboxes |
| "By how many pixels is each element shifted from the reference?" | `align_elements` | per-element `delta: {x, y}` + `improvement` + classification |
| "Is the misalignment a global shift, or per-element drift?" | `align_elements` | groups elements with similar deltas; commits at LCA as `rigid-with-parent` |
| "Two static PNGs, no live page" | `visual_diff` | `Diff: N.NN%` |

**Mechanism difference.** `compare_element`'s `alignTo`/`alignOn` shifts the *reference crop* before scoring (a one-shot offset to the comparison frame). `align_elements` finds a per-element shift via SAD template-matching of the *live* element's pixels against a search window in the reference, then applies CSS `transform: translate(dx, dy)` on the live page so the recovered alignment is visually confirmable. The `compare_element` deltas are inputs you provide; the `align_elements` deltas are outputs the tool computes.

**Trust boundary.** `align_elements` deliberately downplays DOM-reported coordinates. `getBoundingClientRect()` only seeds the search center — the chosen delta is grounded in pixel SAD. Use this when computed-style or `getBoundingClientRect()` numbers are suspect (CSS transforms in the ancestry chain, sub-pixel layout, dynamic positioning libraries, content-visibility quirks). When DOM coordinates are trustworthy, `compare_element` with `alignTo` is faster.

### Coverage contract {#coverage-contract}

Both `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot` and `design_audit` surface coverage metrics, but with different semantics:

- `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot`: **`Mask coverage: N.N%`** — % of the comparison region (cropW × cropH for `compare_element`, full pageImg for `compare_screenshot`) covered by the union of mask regions, dedup-merged via bitmap. 1 decimal precision.
- `design_audit`: **`hiddenArea`** — % of `rootSelector`'s area covered by `hideSelectors` matches, naive sum (no dedup; overlapping selectors over-count). 1 decimal precision.
- `design_audit.coverageManifest`: takes `nodeNames: string[]` and `propertyCounts: {[name]: number}` (typically from figexport's `resolve_styles _meta`); reports per-element coverage stats and unmapped node count. Additional fields produced by upstream tooling (e.g. figexport's `propertyHashes`) are accepted and ignored — browser-mcp does not currently consume them. If a future enforcement check is added, it will be a non-breaking schema extension; producers can pass extras safely today.

Both metrics are percentages, both 1 decimal. Tool-emitted warnings: `maskCoverage > 50%` (generic), `maskCoverage > 60%` with both broad flags (mask-coverage trap fingerprint). `hiddenArea` has no per-call warning; consumers gate it externally.

### Action contract {#action-contract}

`compare_element`, `compare_screenshot`, `design_audit`, and `screenshot` accept `actions: [...]` arrays that run before the capture. Action types:

- `click`, `type`, `hover`, `scroll`, `wait`, `wait_for_selector`, `assert_text`, `assert_count`, `evaluate`, `set_storage`, `set_cookies`, `select_option`, etc.

Assertions inside `actions` produce `assertions` output messages but don't fail the call by themselves. The `evaluate` action is the workaround route for animation-freezing on tools that lack `freezeAnimations` — pass a `<style>` injection that pauses animations and disables transitions.

### Session contract {#session-contract}

- `open_session({ browser, viewport })` returns `session_id`. The session keeps a Playwright `BrowserContext` alive across calls.
- All primitives accept optional `session_id` + `tab_id`. Without `session_id`, the tool spins an ephemeral context per call.
- `close_session({ session_id })` releases the context; `list_sessions()` enumerates active ones.

> **Hazard:** ephemeral sessions cannot accept cookies, storage, or auth state from prior calls — every ephemeral call is a fresh anonymous browser. For multi-step flows that need persistence (login → action → capture), open a session and pass `session_id` to every call.

## Surfaces {#surfaces}

Surface granularity is **per contract**, not per tool. Tools that share a contract (e.g. all four compare tools share the mask contract) point to one section. Tools without a contract entry are routine — see § Command index.

### compare_element {#surface-compare-element}

**Produced by:** `dev` plugin.

**Authoritative for:** live ↔ reference PNG comparison anchored on a CSS selector. Crop window auto-derived from `getBoundingClientRect() + padding` (default 50px). Masking, alignment, coverage reporting all flow through this tool.

**Not authoritative for:** full-page comparisons (use `compare_screenshot`); CSS-property comparisons (use `design_compare`); element-level cross-reference of clusters (use `design_audit`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport / image-pixel (1:1). All inputs (`ignoreRegions`, `alignOn.referenceRect`) and outputs (cluster bboxes, mask region rects) live here.

**Common misreads:**
- *Score reads `Diff: 5%` but `design_audit` reports 0.95* — those are inverse conventions on the same underlying number. `compare_element` reports diff-percent (lower better); `design_audit` reports `visualScore` (higher better). Both are correct.
- *Mask covers most of the crop; score is 99%* — see § Mask contract › mask coverage trap. Re-run unmasked to get the honest score.
- *`alignOn.referenceRect` taken from a non-viewport coordinate frame* — see § Alignment contract › coordinate frame mismatch. Convert first or use `alignTo` for the element-relative shortcut.
- *Crop region exceeds reference image bounds* — pass `boundsHandling: "intersect"` to clamp, or use `alignTo`/`alignOn` to shift the reference origin.

### align_elements {#surface-align-elements}

**Produced by:** `dev` plugin.

**Authoritative for:** per-element pixel-shift measurement against a reference PNG. For each candidate element, finds the integer (dx, dy) such that `transform: translate(dx, dy)` makes the live element's pixels best match the reference, then optionally applies the transforms and captures an aligned screenshot for visual confirmation. Discovers candidates from baseline diff clusters when `selectors` is omitted; tags candidates with a transient `data-align-id` attribute that's stripped before the tool returns.

**Not authoritative for:** percentage-style match scoring (use `compare_element` / `compare_screenshot` / `design_audit` — `align_elements` reports per-pixel SAD, not pixelmatch percent over the whole crop); CSS-property comparisons (use `design_compare`); shifts that aren't pure 2D translations (`scale`, `rotate`, content swaps — see `classification` below).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport / image-pixel (1:1). Live screenshot and reference must have matching dimensions; tool errors out otherwise. Returned `delta.x` / `delta.y` are integer pixel offsets in this frame.

**Search strategy:** the per-element search radius is derived from baseline diff cluster geometry (a 12px-tall red strip can't imply more than ~12px of vertical shift). Default floor 3px, ceiling 60px, auto-grows once if the first pass hits the radius edge. Override with `refineRadius` (floor) and `maxRadius` (ceiling). Score metric is RGB-channel SAD; alpha is ignored.

**Classification.** Each candidate is classified into exactly one of:

- `translation` — clear unique minimum, improvement ≥ `minImprovement` (default 0.005). Transform applied per-element.
- `rigid-with-parent` — this element's delta matches a sibling group's delta within `uniformityTolerance`. The tool finds the lowest common ancestor inside `scope`, applies the shift there, and zeroes the per-element transform. The per-element delta is preserved in the report for diagnostic clarity. LCA is never `body` or `documentElement` — those are skipped to avoid moving content outside the candidate set.
- `content-change` — element diffs but no translation reduces the diff. The element's pixels differ in kind (text content, color, image swap), not position. `align_elements` cannot fix this — switch to `compare_element` or `computed_styles`.
- `size-mismatch` — template / reference crop has zero area or shape mismatch beyond what `translate` can correct. Translation alone cannot align; investigate via `computed_styles`.
- `ambiguous` — a competing minimum within 1.1× of the best score sits ≥ 4px away. Typical of repetitive UI (grid items, lists). The tool reports the best of the tied set; the agent should disambiguate by sibling index or by passing an explicit `selectors` list.
- `no-clusters` — no diff in this element's region; already aligned.

**Common misreads:**
- *Recovered delta is sign-flipped from "what I shifted in the live page"* — by design. The reported delta is the *correction* needed to align live → reference. If a build bug shifts the live element +12px right vs the reference, `align_elements` reports `dx: -12` (the transform needed to undo it).
- *`scope` includes elements outside the page region of interest* — candidates that intersect any baseline cluster anywhere inside `scope` get tagged. Narrow `scope` to a meaningful container (`<main>`, a section selector) when whole-`body` discovery surfaces noise.
- *`applyTransform: true` left visible CSS on the page after the call* — the tool strips `data-align-id` attributes at the end, but transforms persist on the live DOM (intentionally — that's the visual-confirmation channel). If you re-use the same session for further tools, navigate away or hard-reload to clear the inline styles.
- *Image dimensions don't match (hard error)* — same as `compare_screenshot`: viewport must equal reference dimensions. The tool defaults `viewport` to the reference's WxH so this only trips when the agent overrode `viewport` explicitly.
- *Mask flags moved the score but not the deltas* — masks are applied to the SCORING images only, never to the live page or the saved "before" PNG. The masks influence which pixels SAD considers, not where the search happens.

**Mask contract:** identical to `compare_element` — `ignoreImages`, `ignoreBackgrounds`, `ignoreAllImages`, `ignoreText`, `ignoreElements`, `ignoreRegions`. The mask-coverage trap (§ Mask contract) applies: heavily-masked candidates may report spuriously high `improvement`. The tool does not currently emit a coverage warning specific to `align_elements`; check the saved diff PNGs.

**Output artefacts:** `align-before-*.png` (initial screenshot, no transforms), `align-diff-before-*.png` (baseline diff), `align-after-*.png` (post-transform screenshot, present only when `applyTransform: true` and at least one delta was non-zero), `align-diff-after-*.png` (final diff against reference).

### compare_screenshot {#surface-compare-screenshot}

**Produced by:** `dev` plugin.

**Authoritative for:** full-viewport (or `startY`/`endY`-clipped) live ↔ reference PNG comparison, no selector. Mask contract identical to `compare_element`.

**Not authoritative for:** element-anchored crops (use `compare_element`); CSS-property comparisons (use `design_compare`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport / image-pixel.

**Common misreads:**
- *"Image dimensions don't match" hard error* — viewport doesn't match the reference image's WxH. The tool requires equal dims; resize the reference, or use `compare_element` if you only care about a region.
- Same score-convention and mask-coverage-trap misreads as `compare_element`.

### visual_diff {#surface-visual-diff}

**Produced by:** `dev` plugin.

**Authoritative for:** pixelmatch between two static PNGs, no browser launched. Optional `crop: true` auto-crops to the smaller of the two when dimensions differ. Useful as the final step in a manual capture-then-compare flow.

**Not authoritative for:** anything requiring live page state. No mask flags — preprocess the PNGs externally if you need masking.

**Coordinate frame:** image-pixel only.

**Common misreads:**
- *Used to verify a live page change* — `visual_diff` doesn't navigate. Use `compare_screenshot` or `compare_element` for live URL → reference flows.

### design_audit {#surface-design-audit}

**Produced by:** `design-compare` plugin.

**Mode:** none required. `design_audit` does **not** gate on a mode — it runs against any URL the live browser context can reach. It's commonly used inside a session that opted into `wordpress` mode (so authenticated WP admin pages render), but that's a session-context choice, not a tool gate. There is no `design` mode; the design-compare plugin registers tools, not modes.

**Authoritative for:** end-to-end design compliance check. Runs `design_compare` (CSS property comparison) + visual diff + cross-references diff clusters back to named elements. Output groups clusters as `explained` (overlap an element with property mismatches), `excluded` (overlap a `knownExclusions` selector), or `unexplained`. `coverageManifest` enables element/property coverage stats.

**Not authoritative for:** raw pixelmatch (use `compare_screenshot`); element-cropped comparison (use `compare_element`); arbitrary CSS-property check without a design spec (use `computed_styles`).

**Coordinate frame:** HTML viewport. Element bboxes are reported relative to `rootSelector.boundingBox()` (subtracted) for cluster-cross-reference.

**Common misreads:**
- *Looking for `ignoreElements` / `ignoreText` / `ignoreRegions`* — `design_audit` doesn't have them. The analogue is `hideSelectors` (pre-screenshot suppression) and `knownExclusions` (post-hoc cluster classification, no visual effect).
- *`hiddenArea` value used as a fraction* — it's a percentage (1 decimal). Comparing against `0.25` reads it as a quarter of a percent; consumers gating on it should compare against `25`.
- *Cluster cross-reference shows `unexplained` after a fix* — `design_compare` ran before the fix; re-run `design_audit` after the fix and the cluster classification will update.
- *Animation race not caught despite `freezeAnimations: true`* — this flag is `design_audit`-only. If both sides are loaded (e.g. `referenceUrl` for the reference), the flag injects on both. For `compare_*` tools, see § Mask contract › race on animation for the manual workaround.

### design_compare {#surface-design-compare}

**Produced by:** `design-compare` plugin.

**Authoritative for:** CSS-property comparison live ↔ design spec. Tolerant numeric comparison (px tolerance, max 2px cap), color normalization, font-family primary comparison (parses fallback stack), pseudo-element support. No screenshots taken.

**Not authoritative for:** visual / pixel comparison (`design_audit` runs `design_compare` + visual; or use `compare_*` tools); coordinate-based checks beyond `bbox.width` / `bbox.height` (use `evaluate_script` for `getBoundingClientRect()`).

**Coordinate frame:** none — compares CSS values, not coordinates.

**Common misreads:**
- *Tolerance "2px" was passed but a 4px delta is reported as match* — tolerance silently caps at 2px (anti-gaming). The capped value is echoed in the output.
- *Font-family test fails despite the same font* — the comparison parses primary font from fallback stacks via `parseFontStack`. If both sides use the same primary, it matches. For exact-string match, pre-normalize.
- *Position / displacement changes don't move the result* — `design_compare` checks the property list you supplied; if `transform` isn't in the list, displacement is invisible. Use `design_audit`'s visual phase for positional verification.

### list_modes {#surface-list-modes}

**Produced by:** core (always registered, regardless of plugin set).

**Authoritative for:** enumeration of currently registered modes in this server process. Output reflects the env-var-loaded plugin set.

**Not authoritative for:** anything about plugins that aren't loaded. A skipped plugin produces no entry; the tool can't tell you "this would be present if you set `WP_URL`."

**Coordinate frame:** none.

**Common misreads:**
- *"No modes registered"* — see § Diagnosis › Mode not registered. Plugin loader silently skipped one or more plugins for missing env. Stderr has the full list of skips.

## When sources disagree {#when-sources-disagree}

When two sources of truth (live page state, reference image, design spec, prior comparison output) point at different answers, the precedence rule for picking the right tool lives at § Cross-cutting concepts › [Compare-tool selection](#compare-tool-selection). Score-convention reconciliation (diff-percent vs `visualScore`) is in the same subsection. Phenomenon-level disagreements (mask trap, coordinate-frame drift, animation race) are catalogued under § Diagnosis.

## Common workflows {#workflows}

### Compare a built block to a design reference

1. Source the design's expected properties (typically from a figexport-style `resolve_styles` output that produces `nodeNames`, `propertyCounts`, and per-element expected values).
2. Build `elements: [{name, selector, expected}]` from those expected values.
3. Invoke `design_audit({rootSelector, elements, referenceImage, hideSelectors?, knownExclusions?, coverageManifest?})`.
4. Read `visualScore`, per-element results, and cluster cross-reference. Property mismatches surface in `elements[].results`; visual-only misses surface as `unexplained` clusters with `domHints`.

### Investigate a low score

1. Inspect `Mask coverage: N.N%` on `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot` output. If high (and especially if both `ignoreAllImages` and `ignoreText` are active), the score may be a mask-coverage-trap artifact — re-run unmasked.
2. Inspect `clusterAnnotations` — these tell you which DOM elements overlap each diff cluster.
3. For positional claims, use `computed_styles` and `evaluate_script` to read `getBoundingClientRect()` directly on the live element. Reconcile against the design source value, accounting for coordinate-frame conversion (see § Coordinate spaces).
4. If the live and reference agree on element position but the diff persists, look for sibling drivers (an element near the cited one that's actually causing the diff) — `clusterAnnotations` will name them.

### Measure how far off elements are from a reference

1. Capture the reference PNG (or use one supplied by upstream tooling). Reference + viewport must agree on WxH.
2. Invoke `align_elements({url, referenceImage, scope?})`. Default `scope` is `body`; narrow it to the relevant container to suppress noise from unrelated regions.
3. Read the per-element table. `translation` rows give you the (dx, dy) correction. `rigid-with-parent` rows tell you the misalignment is a single-shift error at an ancestor; the report names the ancestor. `content-change` rows tell you the element's *content* differs (text, color, image swap) — `align_elements` can't help, switch tools.
4. If `applyTransform: true` (the default), `align-after-*.png` shows the live page with the recovered transforms applied. Diff this against the reference to confirm; the tool's reported aligned-diff number is the same measurement.
5. To investigate without disturbing the live DOM, pass `applyTransform: false`. The tool still computes deltas and saves the baseline diff; no transforms are applied to the page.

### Open a persistent session for a multi-step flow

1. `open_session({browser: "chromium", viewport: {...}})` → returns `session_id`.
2. Pass `session_id` to every subsequent tool call.
3. `close_session({session_id})` when done. Sessions auto-touch on every call to keep them alive against the idle timeout.

## Diagnosis {#diagnosis}

Generic phenomena that consumers run into. Each entry is named for cross-doc grep — the name describes the phenomenon, not a specific historical case.

Quick symptom lookup:

| Symptom | Phenomenon |
|---|---|
| `list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or an expected mode is absent | [Mode not registered](#mode-not-registered) |
| `Match: YES` / high `visualScore` with visible mismatch on the live page; `Mask coverage: N.N%` is high | [Mask coverage trap](#mask-coverage-trap) |
| `alignOn` warns "delta exceeds 100px," or delta is small but the comparison drifts in a consistent direction across runs | [Coordinate frame mismatch](#coordinate-frame-mismatch) |
| Mask in the diff PNG doesn't line up with the masked element's actual rendered position | [Animation race](#animation-race) |
| `align_elements` reports `ambiguous-minimum` warning, or two distant deltas with similar scores | [Repetitive-UI ambiguity](#repetitive-ui-ambiguity) |
| `align_elements` reports `hit-search-edge` and a delta equal to `maxRadius` | [Search radius too small](#search-radius-too-small) |
| `align_elements` reports `content-change` for elements that visibly look misaligned | [Content vs translation misclassification](#content-vs-translation) |

### Mode not registered {#mode-not-registered}

**Symptom:** `mcp__browser__list_modes` returns "No modes registered" or an expected mode (e.g. `wordpress`) is missing; tools that mode would have provided come back as deferred-but-unresolvable. Or, more subtly: plugin A loaded fine but plugin B (which depends on A) is silently absent.

**Cause:** silent plugin skip from missing env. A plugin with a missing required env var is skipped at load time. Plugins depending on the skipped plugin cascade-skip. The server boots cleanly; affected modes are never registered.

**Fix:** check stderr from server boot for the skip reasons — the cascade is deterministic, so fixing the root cause unblocks all dependents. Add the missing env var to the project's `.mcp.json` (or to `~/.claude.json` for user scope). Remember that MCP scopes replace, not merge — the project entry must duplicate the full env block. Restart Claude Code (a full restart, not `/mcp` reconnect) to pick up env changes.

### Mask coverage trap {#mask-coverage-trap}

**Symptom:** `compare_element` or `compare_screenshot` reports `Match: YES` with low diff percent (or `design_audit` reports a high `visualScore`), but the live page visibly does not match the reference. `Mask coverage: N.N%` is high.

**Cause:** masks obscure most of the comparison region. The remaining unmasked area is uniform across both sides (typically wrapper background) and trivially matches. The combination `ignoreAllImages: true` + `ignoreText: true` on content-heavy regions is the canonical fingerprint, but any mask configuration that exceeds ~60% coverage warrants verification.

**Fix:** re-run with masks removed (or with a narrower set) and read the unmasked score. Treat the unmasked score as the honest measurement; masked-flag invocations are diagnostic isolations, not headline numbers. The tool emits a warning when coverage > 60% with both broad flags; consumers can gate on `Mask coverage: N.N%` directly.

When the consumer's mask configuration is built from upstream design-tooling outputs (e.g. figexport's `masked.json` regions), see `../figexport/llms-full.txt#masked-region-semantics` for what those regions are intended to express — that's the source-side rule that this phenomenon is the consumer-side violation of.

### Coordinate frame mismatch {#coordinate-frame-mismatch}

**Symptom:** `compare_element` `alignOn` reports a delta that exceeds the 100px warning threshold, OR delta is small but the comparison drifts in a consistent direction across runs.

**Cause:** values from a non-viewport coordinate frame (e.g. canvas-relative bboxes from a design source file) were supplied to a viewport-pixel field. The conversion offset between frames absorbs into `deltaX` / `deltaY` and shifts the reference crop. The phenomenon is generic — it applies any time non-viewport coords cross the API boundary, not just on `alignOn.referenceRect`.

**Fix:** convert source coords to HTML viewport pixels before passing them to the tool. The conversion rule for crossing frames lives at § Cross-cutting concepts › Coordinate spaces (and at `../figexport/llms-full.txt#coordinate-spaces` for the upstream-side full treatment). If you only need element-relative alignment, use `alignTo: "top"|"center"` instead of `alignOn` — `alignTo` doesn't take user-supplied coordinates, so it's immune to this class of misread.

### Animation race {#animation-race}

**Symptom:** mask in the diff PNG doesn't line up with the masked element's actual rendered position; pixels that should be masked aren't, or vice versa.

**Cause:** between `compare_element`/`compare_screenshot`'s screenshot capture and its post-screenshot mask-bbox query, an animation or transition fired that moved or resized the masked element. The mask rect describes a position the element no longer occupies in the captured pixels.

**Fix:** stabilize before the capture. Either inject a freeze stylesheet via the `actions` array (`{type: "evaluate", expression: "..."}` adding `*, *::before, *::after { animation-play-state: paused !important; transition: none !important; }`), or pass `delay` greater than the longest transition duration in the block, or use `design_audit`'s `freezeAnimations: true` flag if applicable. Verify by double-capturing — two screenshots taken 1 s apart should diff at ≥ 0.99.

### Repetitive-UI ambiguity {#repetitive-ui-ambiguity}

**Symptom:** `align_elements` reports `[ambiguous]` classification or `ambiguous-minimum` warning on an element. Multiple deltas tied within 1.1× of the best score sit ≥ 4px apart.

**Cause:** the candidate element's pixels appear at multiple plausible positions in the reference window — typical of grid items, repeated icons, list rows. SAD can't tell them apart by pixels alone.

**Fix:** disambiguate structurally rather than visually. Pass an explicit `selectors` list with a more specific selector (e.g. `:nth-of-type(3)` or an `id`-anchored path) so the tool only considers one candidate per visual instance. If the repetition is itself the misalignment (e.g. one card moved into another's slot), `align_elements` is the wrong tool — use `compare_element` per-card with `alignTo` to verify each instance independently.

### Search radius too small {#search-radius-too-small}

**Symptom:** `align_elements` reports `hit-search-edge` warning with a delta equal to `maxRadius` (default 60). The aligned-diff is reduced but not minimized.

**Cause:** the real shift exceeds the search radius. Cluster geometry is supposed to set the radius automatically (a 12px-tall red strip implies ≤ 12px of vertical shift), but baseline diff clustering caps at `topClusters` and a small element near a much larger cluster can hit the ceiling.

**Fix:** raise `maxRadius` (e.g. 120) and re-run. If the shift is genuinely large (> ~100px), DOM-reported coordinates may be the better starting point — use `compare_element` with `alignOn` and a known anchor pair instead. The element being far off-position from where its DOM position implies is itself a finding worth surfacing.

### Content vs translation misclassification {#content-vs-translation}

**Symptom:** `align_elements` classifies an element as `content-change` even though it visually looks misaligned, OR classifies it as `translation` with a small delta when the real bug is a content swap (different text, different image, color shift).

**Cause:** the classifier compares baseline-diff to aligned-diff at the chosen delta. If translation reduces the diff by less than `minImprovement` (default 0.005), the element is labelled `content-change`. If translation reduces the diff a lot but the residual is still high, the label is `translation` even though more is wrong.

**Fix:** read both `improvement` and `alignedDiff` together, not just the classification.
- High `improvement` + low `alignedDiff` → real translation, fix is the reported delta.
- High `improvement` + high `alignedDiff` → translation helps but doesn't finish; there's a content delta layered on top. Run `compare_element` with the recovered delta as `alignTo`-equivalent input to inspect the residual.
- Low `improvement` + high `alignedDiff` → genuine content change. Switch to `compare_element` (for visual diff) or `design_compare` (for property-level checks).

If `minImprovement` looks too aggressive for a particular case (small elements where a 0.005 SAD shift represents meaningful realignment), lower it via the parameter.

## Versioning {#versioning}

This document tracks `browser-mcp` main; for behavior at a specific commit see `git log src/`. Material contract changes (new fields, threshold tweaks, contract additions) update this file in the same PR.
